newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan carmakers' business gradually improving -- S&P.
newsitem.headline: Japan carmakers' business gradually improving -- S&P.

text.p: Japanese carmakers have gradually improved their operating and financial performance over the past two years, Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Friday.
S&P said the improvements reflected stronger domestic demand, stable sales in major overseas markets, a weaker yen, cost-cutting efforts and popular new models.

Although carmakers shifted production overseas to retain competitiveness as the sharp appreciation of the yen through 1995 slowed growth in overseas market share, trade tensions remain a concern for the industry, the ratings agency said.
The overall financial performance of Japanese carmakers improved in the fiscal year to March 31, 1997, mainly due to the weak yen, S&P said.

Toyota Motor Corp and Honda Motor Co Ltd continue to strengthen their business and financial performances, while other carmakers, including Nissan Motor Co Ltd, have not yet seen a substantial improvement beyond currency-related gains.
The gap in financial performance between winners and losers in the industry may widen, S&P said.
